chains.title: CEBPA binds the rs12740374 T allele at a SORT1 enhancer in hepatocytes

links.claim: Alt T binds CEBPA more strongly. QBiC-SELEX group G035 lists CEBPA as an own-model passing member with z 22.63 and the same alt>ref sign as the group best model; E18 shows a CEBPA ChIP-seq peak in HepG2 containing the variant, confirming occupancy but not allele specificity. CEBPA was chosen within the shared C/EBP group because it is the highest-expressed member in the Hep3B2.1-7 expression context and has direct HepG2 ChIP occupancy at the locus.
The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE, EH38E1374646 (dELS), with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal, and overlaps an Ensembl enhancer.

The enhancer is predicted to regulate SORT1: Open Targets L2G ranks SORT1 highest at 0.99, a liver SORT1 sqtl is present with PIP 0.72, and GTEx liver eQTL shows the alt T allele increases SORT1 expression (NES +1.27).

The relevant context is hepatocyte/liver: the provided expression context is Hep3B2.1-7, the SORT1 eQTL is liver-specific, and CEBPA ChIP occupancy is reported in HepG2. This supports but does not prove that hepatocytes are the causal cell type.

The alt T allele is predicted to be protective: E04 reports G as the effect allele for high cholesterol and LDL cholesterol, and E19 shows T associates with higher liver SORT1 expression. The LDL-lowering and MI-protective effect through CEBPA and SORT1 is inferential; MI is not directly tested in the cited rows.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPA ChIP at rs12740374 should show stronger binding on the T allele than on the G allele in a heterozygous hepatocyte line.
CEBPA knockdown or mutation of the C/EBP motif should reduce T-allele enhancer activity and SORT1 expression in hepatocytes.
The T allele should associate with higher SORT1 expression in liver and with lower LDL cholesterol.
falsified_if: Allele-specific CEBPA ChIP in HepG2, Hep3B2.1-7 or liver does not show stronger CEBPA binding on the T allele than on the G allele.
CEBPA knockdown or C/EBP motif mutation does not reduce T-allele enhancer activity or SORT1 expression in a hepatocyte background.
CEBPA occupancy at the rs12740374 enhancer is not reproducible despite the reported HepG2 peak.

grades_v0.reason: QBiC-SELEX is only a binding prediction; no allele-specific ChIP, reporter, MPRA or perturbation is cited. E12 shows CEBPA is an own-model passing member in the C/EBP group with z 22.63, consistent with alt>T binding, but the quoted effect +2.331 is the best-model CEBPB effect, not a CEBPA-specific effect.

E03 directly places the variant in EH38E1374646, a dELS with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal; E01 also annotates an enhancer. Caveat: the chromatin z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not shown for Hep3B2.1-7/hepatocytes.

E05 gives strong genetic support for SORT1 as the target: L2G SORT1 0.99 in multiple credible sets and a liver SORT1 sqtl with PIP 0.72. This is a prediction/gene assignment, not direct enhancer-gene perturbation, and no expression sign is given.

E05 has a liver SORT1 sqtl and E07 uses Hep3B2.1-7 (ACH-000625) as the expression context, consistent with liver relevance. But nothing cited shows that hepatocytes are the causal cell type for this enhancer, and the cCRE activity is not biosample-resolved.

E04 supports association with cholesterol/LDL and has effect allele G for high cholesterol, consistent with T being protective. But E04 also contains an LDL row with effect allele T, so direction is not internally clean; no MI association is cited directly, and no cited evidence shows that T increases SORT1 expression or that SORT1 up-regulation lowers LDL.

E12 directly gives CEBPB as the best model in group G035, z 22.81, effect +2.331, with alt>T and own_model coverage. This is a QBiC-SELEX binding prediction only; no allele-specific ChIP, reporter or perturbation evidence for CEBPB at this variant is cited.
E03 directly places the variant in EH38E1374646, a dELS with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal; E01 also annotates an enhancer. Caveat: z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not hepatocyte-specific.

E05 supports SORT1 as the target by L2G 0.99 and a liver SORT1 sqtl PIP 0.72. This is genetic prediction/colocalisation, not direct enhancer-gene perturbation, and the sign of the effect is not given.
Liver SORT1 sqtl (E05) and the Hep3B2.1-7 expression context (E07) are consistent with liver relevance, but no cited evidence establishes hepatocytes as the causal cell type for this enhancer.

E04 supports cholesterol/LDL association and a G effect allele for high cholesterol, consistent with T protective. However, the LDL row with effect allele T creates a direction caveat, MI is not directly cited, and the causal mediation through CEBPB and SORT1 is assumed rather than shown.
E09 reports CEBPG as an own-model passing TF in group G143, z 26.76, effect +2.321, alt>T. This is QBiC-SELEX prediction only; no experimental allele-specific binding evidence is cited.
E03 directly places the variant in EH38E1374646, a dELS with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal; E01 also annotates an enhancer. Caveat: not biosample-resolved to hepatocytes.
E05 supports SORT1 as the target by L2G 0.99 and a liver SORT1 sqtl PIP 0.72. It does not give the direction of the SORT1 expression or splicing effect.
E05 liver sqtl and E07 Hep3B context support liver relevance, but no evidence shows hepatocytes as the causal cell type for this enhancer and CEBPG in particular.

E04 supports cholesterol/LDL association and a G effect allele for high cholesterol, but the LDL row with effect allele T is a direction caveat, MI is not directly cited, and CEBPG/SORT1 mediation is not shown.

grades_final.reason: QBiC-SELEX group G035 lists CEBPA as an own-model passing member (z 22.63, alt>ref sign) (E12), and E07 confirms the Hep3B2.1-7 expression context, but a SELEX binding change is only a binding prediction. E18 (CEBPA ChIP-seq peak in HepG2 containing the variant) shows occupancy in a liver-derived line but is not allele-specific and is not Hep3B2.1-7. No allelic ChIP, reporter or MPRA at rs12740374 is cited. TF choice is justified (CEBPA is the highest-expressed C/EBP-group member in the context, E12: 141.33 TPM vs CEBPB 4.05, CEBPE 0.0, plus HepG2 occupancy), so this is not an unjustified pick from a SELEX group, but the allele-specific binding claim remains indirect. Coverage status own_model is consistent with E12.

E03 places the variant inside EH38E1374646 (dELS, chr1:109274794-109275142) with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 signal, and E01 independently annotates an ENSR1_CDSQQ enhancer at the site. Caveat: the z-scores given are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not liver-specific, so enhancer activity in hepatocytes is not directly shown; the claim as worded (active dELS, not cell-type-specific) is supported.

Genetics tier: E05 gives L2G SORT1 0.99 with PIP 1.00 credible sets and a liver SORT1 sqtl with PIP 0.72; E19 gives a significant liver eQTL for SORT1 (NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54). E02 places SORT1 123 kb away, consistent with an enhancer-gene assignment. The evidence is variant-to-gene and variant-to-expression, not element-to-gene physical contact, but the claim is framed as 'predicted to regulate SORT1' and is adequately supported for that wording.

Liver relevance is supported (E19 liver eQTL; E07 expression context ACH-000625), but the claim's cell type is hepatocyte/liver and the supporting lines are Hep3B2.1-7/HepG2 (hepatoblastoma-derived) plus bulk liver GTEx, which cannot distinguish hepatocyte from other liver cell types. The claim explicitly hedges ('supports but does not prove'), which matches the evidence; it is indirect rather than direct.

E04 reports G as the effect (risk) allele for high cholesterol (p 9.9e-324), hyperlipidemia and LDLC (p 4.0e-164), so T is the protective allele, matching E19's T-associated increase in liver SORT1 (NES +1.27) and the expected SORT1 direction. Flag: one E04 row ('LDL cholesterol levels', PMID 39414775) lists effect allele T, which is a different effect-allele convention, not a direction reversal, but it should not be quoted as risk-allele evidence; and no MI row is cited even though MI is in the trait list. The chain correctly labels the CEBPA/SORT1 mechanism and the MI-protective inference as inferential, so no over-claim on the mechanistic link.

E12 supplies the strongest SELEX support here: CEBPB is the group best model (z 22.81, effect +2.331, alt>ref) with 3/3 passing models concordant, and E07 confirms expression in ACH-000625. That is still a binding prediction. E20d (PMID 25835000) demonstrates allele-specific C/EBP-beta binding and enhancer activity, but at rs72664324 in the PPAP2B oxLDL enhancer, not at rs12740374 and not in hepatocytes — it is precedent for mechanism, not evidence for this variant. No allelic ChIP/reporter at rs12740374 is cited. Coverage own_model is consistent with E12.

Same as chain_1: E03 places the variant in dELS EH38E1374646 with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 signal and E01 annotates an enhancer at the site. Biosample-specific z-scores are not in the call (values are maxima), so hepatocyte-specific activity is unproven but the element-level claim is directly supported.

E05 (L2G SORT1 0.99, PIP 1.00; liver SORT1 sqtl PIP 0.72) plus E19 (liver SORT1 eQTL NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54) and E02 distance support the variant-to-SORT1 assignment at genetics tier. Note CELSR2 is a close second in L2G (0.96-0.98), so SORT1 ranking highest is supported but not exclusive.

E19 liver eQTL and E07 Hep3B2.1-7 expression context support a liver context, but not hepatocyte specificity; and unlike chain_1 there is no CEBPB occupancy evidence in a liver-derived line (E18 is CEBPA, not CEBPB, and E20d is a macrophage/oxLDL PPAP2B locus). Indirect.

Direction is consistent: E04 G = risk allele for high cholesterol/LDLC, E19 T = higher liver SORT1, so T is protective. Same caveats as chain_1: the single PMID 39414775 'LDL cholesterol levels' row with effect allele T uses a different effect-allele convention, and MI is not directly tested in the cited rows. The chain flags the CEBPB/SORT1 mechanism and MI inference as inferential, so no over-claim.

E09 gives QBiC-SELEX group G143, CEBPG own model, z 26.76, effect +2.321 (alt>ref), and E07 confirms CEBPG expression context (E09 reports 46.37 TPM). This is a binding prediction alone: no ChIP-seq, caQTL, allelic reporter or MPRA evidence for CEBPG is cited, and the chain itself acknowledges 'no experimental occupancy or allele-specific binding evidence.' Also no stated reason for preferring CEBPG over the group's only member beyond SELEX z and expression; that is acceptable as a minimal justification but remains prediction-only. Coverage own_model is consistent with E09.
E03 (dELS EH38E1374646 with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 signal) and E01 (Ensembl enhancer) directly support the element claim; caveat that z-scores are biosample maxima rather than liver-specific.

E05 (L2G SORT1 0.99, PIP 1.00; liver SORT1 sqtl PIP 0.72), E19 (liver SORT1 eQTL NES +1.27) and E02 distance support the variant-to-SORT1 assignment. CELSR2 is nearly tied in L2G (0.96-0.98), which is a caveat to exclusivity but not to the claim as worded.

Liver context is supported by E19 and E07, but hepatocyte specificity is not: no CEBPG occupancy in any liver-derived line is cited, and the chain's own binding step notes the absence of occupancy evidence. Indirect/context-only.

E04 G risk allele for high cholesterol/LDLC and E19 T-associated higher liver SORT1 give a consistent protective direction for T. Same caveats: PMID 39414775's effect-allele-T LDLC row is a convention difference, not a direction reversal, and MI is untested in the cited rows. The rescue of the phenotype to CEBPG specifically is inferential and the chain says so; residual concern is that CEBPG is the least-supported TF link (prediction only) yet carries the same phenotype confidence — acceptable because the phenotype claim does not depend on CEBPG being the effector.

checks.why: Tests whether CEBPA actually occupies this enhancer in a hepatocyte-derived line; a negative result would strongly weaken the CEBPA chain, though ChIP-seq alone would not establish allele specificity.
Provides the sign of the SORT1 eQTL in liver. If the T allele does not associate with higher SORT1 expression, the proposed binding-to-expression-to-LDL direction fails.
Searches for direct allele-specific reporter, MPRA or ChIP evidence at rs12740374 for C/EBP factors, which is the main missing perturbation-level support across all three chains.
